summary: Validity is the XOR parity of all n input bits. Every bit can change the answer, yielding an Omega(n) inspection lower bound that the accepted single-pass fold matches.

optimality.argument: A correct algorithm must inspect all n derived bits because changing any one bit flips validity, while the accepted solution performs one constant-time XOR per bit.

replacement_checks.evidence: For any uninspected position, flipping only that derived bit flips the total XOR and therefore flips validity; a correct worst-case algorithm must inspect all n positions.
The accepted solution visits each derived entry once, performs one constant-time XOR, and stores only one parity bit, establishing O(n) time and O(1) space.
Cases cover length one, valid and invalid pairs, all zeros, even and odd counts of set bits, and circular arrays of several lengths.
